chmmc-cmm-2024-ib-qual-04.title: Substitute $u=1/x$
chmmc-cmm-2024-ib-qual-04.body:
With $u=\frac1x$, $du=-\frac{dx}{x^2}$; the limits $x=1,\infty$ become $u=1,0$. So the integral is $\int_0^1e^u\,du=e-1$.

**Answer: $e-1$**

chmmc-cmm-2024-ib-qual-05.title: Substitute $u=x^2$
chmmc-cmm-2024-ib-qual-05.body:
With $u=x^2$, $du=2x\,dx$ and the upper limit becomes $2^{-1/2}$, so the integral is $\int_0^{1/\sqrt2}\frac{du}{\sqrt{1-u^2}}=\arcsin\frac1{\sqrt2}=\frac\pi4$.

**Answer: $\frac\pi4$**

chmmc-cmm-2024-ib-qual-06.title: Two triangles
chmmc-cmm-2024-ib-qual-06.body:
The graph of $|x-3|$ on $[0,6]$ consists of two right triangles with base $3$ and height $3$, each of area $\frac92$. Total $9$.

**Answer: 9**

chmmc-cmm-2024-ib-qual-07.title: Odd part vanishes
chmmc-cmm-2024-ib-qual-07.body:
Split into $\int_{-2}^2\frac{4}{4+x^2}dx+\int_{-2}^2\frac{\sin2x}{4+x^2}dx$. The second integrand is odd, so its integral over $[-2,2]$ is $0$. For the first, $\frac4{4+x^2}=\frac1{1+(x/2)^2}$ has antiderivative $2\arctan\frac x2$, giving $2\left(\frac\pi4+\frac\pi4\right)=\pi$.

**Answer: $\pi$**

chmmc-cmm-2024-ib-qual-08.title: Simplify the continued fraction
chmmc-cmm-2024-ib-qual-08.body:
$1+\frac1x=\frac{x+1}x$, so $\frac1{1+1/x}=\frac x{x+1}$. Then $1+\frac x{x+1}=\frac{2x+1}{x+1}$ and the integrand is $\frac{x+1}{2x+1}=\frac12+\frac1{2(2x+1)}$.

Integrating from $0$ to $1$: $\frac12+\frac14\ln(2x+1)\Big|_0^1=\frac12+\frac{\ln3}4=\frac12\left(1+\frac{\ln3}2\right)$.

**Answer: $\frac12+\frac{\ln3}4$**

chmmc-cmm-2024-ib-qual-09.title: Integration by parts
chmmc-cmm-2024-ib-qual-09.body:
Let $x=e^u$: the integral becomes $\int_1^2\left(\ln u+\frac1u\right)e^u\,du$. Integrating $e^u\ln u$ by parts gives $\left[e^u\ln u\right]_1^2-\int_1^2\frac{e^u}u\,du$, which cancels the other term exactly. The value is $e^2\ln2-e\ln1=e^2\ln2$.

**Answer: $e^2\ln2$**

chmmc-cmm-2024-ib-qual-09.title: Product rule
chmmc-cmm-2024-ib-qual-09.body:
$\frac{d}{dx}\left(x\ln\ln x\right)=\ln\ln x+\frac1{\ln x}$, so the integral is $\left[x\ln\ln x\right]_e^{e^2}=e^2\ln2-e\ln1=e^2\ln2$.

**Answer: $e^2\ln2$**

chmmc-cmm-2024-ib-qual-10.title: Sum of cubes
chmmc-cmm-2024-ib-qual-10.body:
With $s=x+x^{-1}$, $s^3=x^3+3x+3x^{-1}+x^{-3}$, so $x^3+x^{-3}=s^3-3s$ and the integrand is $s^2-3=x^2+x^{-2}-1$. Then $\int_1^2\left(x^2+x^{-2}-1\right)dx=\left[\frac{x^3}3-\frac1x-x\right]_1^2=\left(\frac83-\frac12-2\right)-\left(\frac13-1-1\right)=\frac{11}6$.

**Answer: $\frac{11}6$**

chmmc-cmm-2024-ib-qual-12.title: Reverse product rule
chmmc-cmm-2024-ib-qual-12.body:
Seek $g$ with $g+g'=\tan x+\tan^2x-x=(\tan x-x)+(\sec^2x-1)$. Taking $g=\tan x-x$ gives $g'=\sec^2x-1$, so the integrand is $\left(e^x(\tan x-x)\right)'$. The value is $e(\tan1-1)-0$.

**Answer: $e(\tan1-1)$**

chmmc-cmm-2024-ib-qual-13.title: Substitute and use $\tan^2=\sec^2-1$
chmmc-cmm-2024-ib-qual-13.body:
With $u=2\theta-1$: $\frac12\int_{-1}^{\pi/2-1}\tan^2u\,du=\frac12\left[\tan u-u\right]_{-1}^{\pi/2-1}$. Using $\tan\left(\frac\pi2-1\right)=\cot1$, this is $\frac12\left[\left(\cot1-\frac\pi2+1\right)-(-\tan1+1)\right]=\frac12\left[\cot1+\tan1-\frac\pi2\right]$. Since $\cot1+\tan1=\frac1{\sin1\cos1}=\frac2{\sin2}$, the value is $\frac1{\sin2}-\frac\pi4=\csc2-\frac\pi4$.

**Answer: $\csc2-\frac\pi4$**

chmmc-cmm-2024-ib-qual-14.title: Weierstrass substitution
chmmc-cmm-2024-ib-qual-14.body:
Let $t=\tan\frac\theta2$, so $\cos\theta=\frac{1-t^2}{1+t^2}$, $d\theta=\frac{2dt}{1+t^2}$ and $t$ runs over $[0,1]$. The integral becomes $\int_0^1\frac{2\,dt}{(\sqrt2+1)t^2+(\sqrt2-1)}=\int_0^1\frac{2(\sqrt2-1)\,dt}{t^2+(\sqrt2-1)^2}$ (multiplying numerator and denominator by $\sqrt2-1$) $=2\arctan\frac t{\sqrt2-1}\Big|_0^1=2\arctan(\sqrt2+1)$.

Since $\tan\frac{3\pi}8=1+\sqrt2$, this equals $2\cdot\frac{3\pi}8=\frac{3\pi}4$.

**Answer: $\frac{3\pi}4$** (the official answer is written $2\arctan(\sqrt2+1)$, the same number)
